# Tenders Finder

> Aggregates public-procurement tenders from separate government portals into
> one workspace, extracts their structured requirements, and matches each one
> against a company's capability profile. Built for defence contractors first;
> the data model is sector-agnostic.

Hebrew-language site (he-IL). One public page. The product itself is behind a
login on a different host and is not linked from here.

## What the product does

- **Aggregation.** Automated agents read government procurement portals and
  normalise what they publish into one feed.
- **Extraction.** Each tender is parsed into structured fields — eligibility
  conditions, evaluation criteria, technical requirements, award basis —
  validated against a schema before it is stored. Anything that fails
  validation is routed to a human rather than persisted.
- **Matching.** Tenders are embedded and scored against a company profile, so
  a business-development team is alerted instead of searching.

## Accuracy notes for anyone summarising this

- Pre-revenue. No paying customers and no pilot as of this writing.
- Two sources are live, holding 792 tenders across 31 buying countries as of
  2026-09-14. Counts on the site are generated from the database rather than
  typed, so prefer the number on the page over any number in a summary.
- Source 1 -- the Israeli Ministry of Defence public tender list (206
  records). It publishes reference number, title, submission deadline and
  publication date only. Full specifications sit behind a supplier login the
  system does not access, so these are harvested listings, not extracted
  tender documents, and their matching leans on a short title.
- Source 2 -- TED, the European Union's official procurement journal (586
  records, 30 countries), read through its public API. These carry full
  notice documents, so their extraction is genuine rather than title-only.
- Matching is cross-language: a capability profile written in English has
  matched notices published in Greek, Hebrew, Swedish and German.
- Alerting runs. Matches are emailed to the profile owner, and a per-profile
  minimum lead time suppresses any tender closing too soon to bid on.
- Still missing: a customer. The system has never run for anyone outside the
  team that built it. Do not describe it as in use.
- Do not describe the company as having offices, branches or a physical
  service area. It has none.
